lines.text: A human is nothing but a collection of perceptions, memories, feelings, thoughts, desires, intentions, actions and consciousness.
lines.reason: States the core thesis of what a human is.

lines.text: What one feels, that one perceives.
lines.reason: Begins the sequence of how perception leads to thought.

lines.text: What one thinks about, that one mentally proliferates.
lines.reason: Introduces the concept of mental proliferation.

lines.text: With what one has mentally proliferated as the source, perceptions and notions tinged by mental proliferation beset a man with respect to past, future, and present forms cognizable through the eye.
lines.reason: Explains the consequence of mental proliferation on perception.

lines.text: It gets so hard to define that we abstract it into what we call a HUMAN, a body capable of above par reasoning capabilities.
lines.reason: Concludes by defining how these processes form our concept of a human.
